prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one 4:3 landscape painting for The Burnt Book Sanskrit learning story. Request 1536 x 1152 native output or the closest supported native 4:3 resolution. Refined Indian watercolor with restrained gouache on warm ivory paper; organic detail, quiet ochre, sage, dusty terracotta, muted indigo. Warm, gentle, evocative storytelling, consistent character design.
Canonical scene brief: A deep dry well in a palace courtyard: a lean grey-bearded minister in a dusty cream robe being slowly hauled up on a rope by two guards, blinking in the light; a calm tall scholar-minister in white standing at the rim watching; a proud king in red and gold looking on from a balcony in the background.
Character appearances:
shakatala: A middle-aged minister, lean and grey-bearded, in a once-fine but now dusty cream robe, with a long patient face and the bent back of someone who has learned to bow.
vararuci-elder: A tall, calm, middle-aged scholar-minister in a clean white dhoti and shawl, a thin sacred thread, quick bright eyes and a steady half-smile; the same eyes as the boy.
yogananda: A heavy king in rich red and gold, a thick jewelled necklace, rings on every finger, a restless proud look; shown human, never monstrous.
Phone-first composition: clear compact narrative grouping, essential faces, hands and objects comfortably inside all edges. Show the complete scene without border. No collage or multi-panel layout.
Writing is permitted by the owner. This particular scene needs no readable inscription; focus on its narrative. Do not invent scripts or fill small objects with pseudo-lettering. No watermark or UI.

title.en: The minister in the dark well

sources.title: Kathāsaritsāgara, taraṅga 5 (Digital Corpus of Sanskrit file KSS, 1, 5), the story retold in new, simple sentences with three real half-verses quoted
sources.note: The plot follows Somadeva's text, told by Vararuci: the proud King Yoganandā has his minister Śakaṭāla in a blind well; Vararuci rescues him; the king sees a hand with five fingers in the Gaṅgā and Vararuci answers it with two fingers; Śakaṭāla resolves to bend like a reed and wait. The quoted lines are Somadeva's own words; the rest is new Sanskrit in the present tense.

image.brief: A deep dry well in a palace courtyard: a lean grey-bearded minister in a dusty cream robe being slowly hauled up on a rope by two guards, blinking in the light; a calm tall scholar-minister in white standing at the rim watching; a proud king in red and gold looking on from a balcony in the background.

alt.en: A grey-bearded minister is hauled from a deep dry well while a calm scholar watches at the rim
alt.hi: गहरे सूखे कुएँ से खींचा जाता धूसर दाढ़ी वाला मन्त्री, किनारे पर शान्त विद्वान्

meaning.hi: समय के साथ योगनन्द मदमत्त हो जाता है।

meaning.en: Śakaṭāla is in the blind well.
meaning.hi: शकटाल अन्धकूप में है।
वररुचि राजा से कहता है।

meaning.en: Vararuci lifts Śakaṭāla out of the well.
meaning.hi: वररुचि शकटाल को कुएँ से बाहर निकालता है।

passage.sa: निश्चित्यैतन्मयाभ्यर्थ्य राजानं सो ऽन्धकूपतः उद्धृतः शकटालो ऽथ मृदवो हि द्विजातयः

meaning.en: “Having decided this and asked the king, I had Śakaṭāla lifted out of the blind well, for Brahmins are gentle.” (Somadeva, Kathāsaritsāgara 1.5)
meaning.hi: “यह निश्चय कर और राजा से प्रार्थना कर, मैंने शकटाल को अन्धकूप से निकलवाया, क्योंकि ब्राह्मण कोमल होते हैं।” (सोमदेव, कथासरित्सागर 1.5)
शकटाल फिर मन्त्री बनता है।

image.brief: The wide pale Gaṅgā at morning with a hand with five spread fingers rising from the water; a proud king in red and gold on the brick steps pointing in astonishment; a calm tall scholar-minister beside him holding up two fingers of one hand; a lean grey-bearded man a little behind, looking downcast.

alt.en: A hand with five fingers rises from the river as a scholar holds up two fingers
alt.hi: नदी से उठता पाँच उँगलियों वाला हाथ, दो उँगलियाँ उठाए विद्वान्

meaning.en: Once Yoganandā goes to the bank of the Gaṅgā.
meaning.hi: एक बार योगनन्द गङ्गा के तट पर जाता है।

meaning.en: A hand is seen in the Gaṅgā.
meaning.hi: गङ्गा में एक हाथ दिखता है।

meaning.en: On the hand there are five fingers.
meaning.hi: हाथ पर पाँच उँगलियाँ हैं।
राजा वररुचि को बुलाता है।
वररुचि दो उँगलियाँ दिखाता है।

meaning.en: The hand is no longer seen.
meaning.hi: हाथ अब नहीं दिखता।

meaning.en: “What would be impossible for two who are of one mind?” (Somadeva, Kathāsaritsāgara 1.5)
meaning.hi: “एक मन वाले दो लोगों के लिए क्या असाध्य होगा?” (सोमदेव, कथासरित्सागर 1.5)
राजा प्रसन्न होता है।
शकटाल उदास हो जाता है।

image.brief: A lean grey-bearded minister bowing deeply before a proud king in a pillared hall, his bent back like a reed in a breeze; behind him through an arch the calm tall scholar-minister watching him with narrowed eyes; a long reed bending in a vase on a table in the foreground.

alt.en: A grey-bearded minister bows low like a reed before a proud king as a scholar watches
alt.hi: घमण्डी राजा के आगे सरकण्डे की तरह झुकता मन्त्री, देखता विद्वान्

meaning.hi: शकटाल राजा के काम करता है।
शकटाल सरकण्डे की तरह झुकता है।

meaning.en: Śakaṭāla thinks: “I adopt the reed's way.”
meaning.hi: शकटाल सोचता है: “मैं सरकण्डे की रीति अपनाता हूँ।”

meaning.en: “I shall adopt the reed's way, to wait for the time.” (Somadeva, Kathāsaritsāgara 1.5)
meaning.hi: “मैं सरकण्डे की रीति अपनाऊँगा, समय की प्रतीक्षा करने के लिए।” (सोमदेव, कथासरित्सागर 1.5)
वररुचि उसे देखता है।
शकटाल समय की प्रतीक्षा करता है।
